definitions.gloss: various foreign countries; other countries; foreign nations
definitions.explanation: A collective term referring to multiple foreign countries, often used when comparing Japan with other nations or discussing international trends.

examples.japanese: {諸外国|しょがいこく}と{比|くら}べてみる。
{諸外国|しょがいこく}の{事例|じれい}を{参考|さんこう}にすべきだ。
examples.english: We should refer to examples from other countries.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{教育|きょういく}{制度|せいど}は{諸外国|しょがいこく}と{比較|ひかく}して{独自|どくじ}の{特徴|とくちょう}がある。
examples.english: Japan's education system has unique features compared with those of other countries.

notes:
Composed of {諸|しょ} (various, many) + {外国|がいこく} (foreign countries). The prefix {諸|しょ} adds the meaning of "various" or "several," making this a formal way to refer to multiple foreign nations collectively.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {諸外国|しょがいこく}と{比較|ひかく}する (to compare with other countries)
- {諸外国|しょがいこく}の{制度|せいど} (systems of other countries)
- {諸外国|しょがいこく}に{遅|おく}れを{取|と}る (to lag behind other countries)
- {諸外国|しょがいこく}から{学|まな}ぶ (to learn from other countries)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {外国|がいこく} — foreign country; singular or general, less formal
- {海外|かいがい} — overseas; broader term that can include regions, not just countries
- {各国|かっこく} — each country, every country; emphasizes individual countries rather than a collective group

USAGE:
{諸外国|しょがいこく} is a formal expression common in news, policy discussions, and academic writing. It is almost always used from a Japanese perspective, comparing Japan with other nations. It implies a serious, analytical tone.
